Body: Similar to the first test, this manually creates test directories and expects the Log module to use them, but the Log module will use `Global.Path.log` from the XDG-based test isolation. The test should rely on the existing test infrastructure instead of creating its own directory structure.

The cleanup function is async but is not awaited here. This means the init function will return before cleanup completes, potentially causing race conditions where log files are deleted after the function appears to have finished. Change this to `await cleanup(Global.Path.log)` and ensure the init function signature remains async.
```suggestion
    await cleanup(Global.Path.log)
```

Same issue as the first test: `print: true` causes early return without creating log files or running cleanup. This test won't actually validate log rotation behavior. Use `print: false` or omit the print option to test the actual cleanup/rotation logic.

The test manually creates a `.test-log` directory in the current working directory, but the actual Log module uses `Global.Path.log` which is already configured for test isolation via XDG environment variables in test/preload.ts. This test should rely on the existing test isolation setup instead of creating its own directory structure. The manual directory creation could interfere with other tests and leaves cleanup dependent on test success. Remove the manual directory setup and let the Log module use the pre-configured isolated test paths.

The note states that these aliases "will automatically fetch the latest version each time you run them," but this is not entirely accurate. Both `npx` and `bunx` cache packages locally and will not fetch the latest version on every run. They typically check for updates but may use cached versions. To ensure the latest version is always used, users would need to periodically clear their cache or use additional flags. Consider revising the note to clarify this behavior, such as: "These aliases will check for and download the latest version when available. To force a fresh download, you may need to clear your package cache."
```suggestion
> These aliases will check for and download the latest version when available. To force a fresh download, you may need to clear your package cache. Use `opencode-dev` to test the latest development branch features.
```

The documentation shows both Bun and npm alias definitions using the same alias names (`opencode` and `opencode-dev`). Since shell aliases with the same name would conflict, users must choose one set or the other, not both. Consider adding a clarifying note such as "Choose either the Bun or npm aliases below (not both)" to prevent confusion and avoid users accidentally adding conflicting aliases to their shell configuration.

But in my opinion, this currently doesn't correctly support [multi-project structures](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/multi_project_builds_intermediate.html#sec:project_structure), as it would detect a subproject/module as root.

I would suggest:

  // 1) Nearest Gradle root (multi-project or included build)
  NearestRoot(["settings.gradle.kts", "settings.gradle"])(start) ??
  // 2) Gradle wrapper (strong root signal)
  NearestRoot(["gradlew", "gradlew.bat"])(start) ??
  // 3) Single-project or module-level build
  NearestRoot(["build.gradle.kts", "build.gradle"])(start) ??
  // 4) Maven fallback
  NearestRoot(["pom.xml"])(start),
```

The new `extraBody` feature lacks test coverage. Consider adding tests to verify:
1. Provider-level `extraBody` is correctly merged into the result
2. Model-level `extraBody` is correctly merged into the result  
3. Model-level `extraBody` takes precedence over provider-level when keys overlap
4. Empty `extraBody` objects don't add properties to the result
5. Edge cases like undefined or non-object values are handled correctly

The existing test file at `packages/opencode/test/provider/transform.test.ts` has comprehensive tests for the `ProviderTransform.options` function that you can use as a reference.

The `extraBody` properties are being merged twice, which will cause duplicate properties in the final options object. 

When `model.options.extraBody` is defined:
1. Line 468-471 extracts and flattens `extraBody` properties into the top level of `result`
2. In `llm.ts` line 90, the entire `model.options` (including the nested `extraBody` object) is merged again via `mergeDeep`

This means the final options object will contain both the flattened properties AND the nested `extraBody` object. For example, if `model.options = { extraBody: { foo: "bar" } }`, the result will have both `foo: "bar"` at the top level and `extraBody: { foo: "bar" }` as a nested object.

Consider either:
1. Not merging `model.options` again in `llm.ts` after it's already been processed in `ProviderTransform.options()`, OR
2. Excluding the `extraBody` key when merging `model.options` in `llm.ts` (e.g., using `omit` from remeda)

    const extraBody = { ...(providerOptions?.extraBody ?? {}) }
    if (Object.keys(extraBody).length > 0) {
      // Merge in extra body options from providerOptions only
```

My recommendation (and what's somewhat conventional) is the app implementation is responsible for setting up this exporter machinery and then if the app is using a library that has an existing otel instrumentation, you enable that. For example ai-sdk provides otel instrumentation. If you use the openai sdk or claude sdk directly, you'd leverage that instrumentation.

The main issue I could imaging (assuming you don't want to be churning on setting all the attributes to work well across vendors) is that the attribute naming for llm related spans is still a bit of a mess as everyone is trying to figure out how to consistently name all these attributes.

If you're just collecting traces for performance sake and don't care about llm/eval then all these traces will show up just fine with the span `operation.name`s you've defined in any trace viewer. The use case I mostly care about is shipping the signals to a tool like langfuse. Those tools expect specific names to show things like sessionID, llm generation, tool call etc.

The different vendors a re working on making the core attributes more uniform but it's not there yet, so personally, I'd try and punt most of that churn on to something like the ai sdk.

Here's a quick snapshot of the landscape of attribute definitions
- Openllmetry has a reasonable collection here https://github.com/traceloop/openllmetry/blob/main/packages/opentelemetry-semantic-conventions-ai/opentelemetry/semconv_ai/__init__.py
- Here's what ai-sdk collects https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-core/telemetry#collected-data
- Langfuse span operation types https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/observation-types and trace attributes https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry#trace-level-attributes
- The emerging OTEL semantic conventions (still very incomplete) 
  - https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/
  - https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans/ e.g. operation types still don't have a standard naming here yet.

Missing "flex" class in the classList. The "flex-col" class only sets flex-direction to column, but "flex" is required to enable flexbox display. Without it, the layout may not render correctly. Add "flex" to the static classes.
```suggestion
        "relative w-full flex flex-col border-t border-border-weak-base": true,
```

The classList includes "flex-col" but is missing the "flex" class. The "flex-col" directive requires the element to have "display: flex" applied, which is done via the "flex" class in Tailwind. Without it, the flex-col class will not have the intended effect. The "flex-1" class (when fullHeight is true) does apply "flex: 1 1 0%", but doesn't set "display: flex".
```suggestion
        "relative w-full flex flex-col border-t border-border-weak-base": true,
```

This will cause the decoding to fail or produce incorrect results. The check should be `!dir` only, or use the raw params.dir for the second decode.

The AgentTerminalTab component is a regular function component that returns JSX conditionally, but it doesn't check if the agentTerminal context is available. If the component is rendered in a different context where AgentTerminalProvider is not in the hierarchy, calling useAgentTerminal() will throw an error. However, since the component is only used within the Session page which is wrapped with AgentTerminalProvider, this is acceptable. Consider adding a comment explaining this dependency.

Using innerHTML with ANSI-to-HTML conversion could introduce XSS vulnerabilities if the command output contains malicious content that bypasses the ANSI parser's escapeXML option. While escapeXML is set to true in the AnsiToHtml configuration, verify that the ansi-to-html library properly sanitizes all HTML entities and special characters. Consider adding an additional sanitization layer or documenting the security assumptions.

The auto-scroll effect tracks changes to the commands array but should also track changes to the output content of individual commands. When a running command streams output, the commands array reference may not change (only the output property within a command), which means the effect won't trigger and scrolling won't occur during streaming. Consider tracking a more specific dependency that captures output changes, such as combining the commands with their output lengths or using a separate effect that runs on any command state change.

The getBackgroundColor function is called on every render instead of being memoized. Since it accesses theme data that may change infrequently, this creates unnecessary re-computations. Wrap this function with createMemo to improve performance and only recompute when theme-related values change.

The ANSI converter is recreated on every theme change, but a new AnsiToHtml instance is created every time the memo runs. This includes mutating the colors object that comes from defaultColors. The colors object should be cloned before mutation to avoid side effects, or the entire colors object should be built fresh each time without mutation.

Each call to `init()` pushes new unsubscribe functions without clearing existing ones. Consider adding a check to prevent re-initialization or call `dispose()` at the start of `init()` to clean up any existing subscriptions.

There's a potential race condition between the timeout callback (lines 52-58) and the response handler (lines 36-46). If a response arrives at exactly the same time as the timeout fires, both could execute simultaneously. While the current implementation uses Map.get() and Map.delete() which should handle this, consider checking if the request still exists after clearTimeout to make the race handling more explicit.

The new cleanup methods (remove, size, clear) are not being called anywhere in the production code. While they provide the infrastructure for memory management, the PR doesn't include integration points where these methods would actually be invoked (e.g., when an ACP connection closes or a session is terminated). Consider adding calls to sessionManager.remove() in the appropriate lifecycle hooks, such as the cancel method or connection cleanup handlers.

The FileTime.clearSession() method is not being called anywhere in the production code. While the method provides the infrastructure for memory management, there are no integration points where it would actually be invoked when a session ends. Consider adding calls to FileTime.clearSession() in session cleanup handlers or when sessions are removed.

The timeout cleanup only runs when a timeout occurs, but expired transports can accumulate if OAuth flows are abandoned before timeout. Consider implementing periodic cleanup or cleanup on every insertion to handle abandoned flows more proactively. For example, running cleanup on a timer or on every state initialization would prevent accumulation of entries that never timeout.

After calling finishAuth on the transport (line 822), the entry is deleted from pendingOAuthTransports at line 840 before the subsequent add() operation. If the add() call or any other operation fails after line 840, the transport is already removed and cannot be retried. Consider moving the deletion to after the entire operation succeeds to allow retry on partial failures.

The break statement in the finally block will cause the event subscription loop to terminate after processing only the first event, regardless of event type. This means subsequent events for the session will never be processed. The break statements on lines 168 and 372 should be removed.

The abort signal check at line 117 only prevents processing events that have already been received. The for-await loop will continue waiting for the next event from events.stream even after controller.abort() is called, potentially keeping the subscription alive indefinitely. Consider passing the AbortController signal to the subscribe() call if the SDK supports it, or ensure the stream is properly closed when the controller is aborted.

The dispose method doesn't prevent further operations on this agent instance after disposal. If any async operations (like event handling or permission requests) are still in flight when dispose() is called, they may attempt to use this.connection or this.sessionManager after they've been cleared, potentially causing errors. Consider adding checks for this.disposed before accessing these resources in async operations, or rejecting pending operations when disposing.
Fixed in 42fea26: Moved break outside finally blocks, added proper catch blocks.

Fixed in 42eaef3: The SDK does support a `signal` option - now passing `{ signal: controller.signal }` to `subscribe()`. The SSE client registers an abort handler that calls `reader.cancel()` to properly close the stream when aborted.

Fixed in 2c7ac10: Added `this.disposed` checks:
1. At the start of each event case (`if (this.disposed) break`)
2. After key `await` calls (`if (this.disposed) return`)

This ensures in-flight async operations exit gracefully rather than continuing to use potentially invalid resources after disposal.
